{{Short description|Dutch mathematician (1939–2022)}}
'''Gerrit van Dijk''' (14 August 1939, [[Kampen, Overijssel]] – 16 April 2022) was a Dutch professor of [[mathematics]] and [[physics]]. In 2004 he was appointed an Officer of the [[Order of Orange-Nassau]].<ref name=memoriam>{{cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/news/2022/04/in-memoriam-g.-van-dijk |title=In Memoriam Emeritus Professor G. Van Dijk |date=22 April 2022 |website=Leiden University}}</ref>

==Biography==
Van Dijk studied mathematics at [[Utrecht University]], where he received his PhD in 1969 with thesis advisor [[T. A. Springer]].<ref name=MathGen>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=49665|name=Gerrit van Dijk}}</ref> As a postdoc, van Dijk worked for the academic year 1969–1970 in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Gerrit van Dijk|website=Institute for Advanced Study (ias.edu)|date=9 December 2019 |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/gerrit-van-dijk}}</ref> There he was inspired by [[Harish-Chandra]] to study [[harmonic analysis]] with the [[representation theory]] of [[Lie group]]s<ref name=memoriam/> and prepared the notes for Harish-Chandra's 1969 monograph ''Harmonic analysis on reductive p-adic groups''.<ref>{{cite book|author=Harish-Chandra|title=Harmonic analysis on reductive p-adic groups|year=1970|postscript=; iv+125 pages; notes by G. van Dijk|location=Berlin; New York|publisher=Springer-Verlag|lccn=79138810}}</ref> From 1970 to 1972 van Dijk was a staff member at Utrecht University. At [[Leiden University]] he was appointed lecturer in 1972 and was promoted to professor in 1980. From 1988 to 1992 he was Leiden University's [[dean (education)|dean]] of the faculty of mathematics and natural sciences. He was from 1995 to 1997 he was the director of Leiden University's Lorenz Center<ref name=memoriam/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lorentzcenter.nl/history-in-brief.html |title=History in brief |website=Lorentz Center, Universiteit Leiden}}</ref> and from 1997 to 2004 the director of Leiden University's Mathematical Institute. From 2003 to 2004 he directed the Leiden Institute for Advanced Computer Science (LIACS). He was a professor at Leiden University until 2004, when he retired as professor emeritus.<ref name=memoriam/>

Van Dijk was a visiting professor at various universities in several countries: Germany (Göttingen), France (Nancy), Japan (Fukuoka), Russia (Tambov), and Sweden (Stockholm). He was a member of the [[Royal Dutch Mathematical Society]], the [[Batavian Society for Experimental Philosophy]], and the ''[[Koninklijke Hollandsche Maatschappij der Wetenschappen]]''. He supervised 14 doctoral dissertations (some of them with [[Tom Koornwinder]]). Van Dijk did research on Lie groups, p-adic representation theory, harmonic analysis, [[symmetric space]]s, [[homogeneous space]]s, [[Gelfand pair]]s,  and [[Berezin transform]]s with generalizations.<ref name=memoriam/><ref name=AMSnews>{{cite web|title=Gerrit van Dijk (1939-2022)|date=May 3, 2022|url=http://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7020 | website=News from the AMS, American Mathematical Society }}</ref> His collaborators include Vladimir Fedorovich Molchanov,<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/S0021-7824(99)80011-7|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021782499800117 |title=Tensor products of maximal degenerate series representations of the group SL(n, R) |date=1999 |last1=Van Dijk |first1=G. |last2=Molchanov |first2=V.F. |journal=Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées |volume=78 |pages=99–119 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[Masato Wakayama]], Tom Koornwinder, and Erik G. F. Thomas.<ref name=memoriam/> Van Dijk's doctoral students include Gerrit Heckman and [[Eric Opdam]]<ref name=MathGen/> (known for [[Heckman–Opdam polynomials]]).

Van Dijk did historical research on the life and work of the 19th-century Dutch mathematician [[Thomas Joannes Stieltjes]], as well as other Leiden mathematics professors from the past. This research work resulted in a new issue of Stieltjes's collected works, a portrait gallery in Leiden University's Mathematical Institute, and publication of the book ''Leidse hoogleraren Wiskunde 1575-1975'', which documents the lives of about forty Leiden mathematics professors.<ref name=AMSnews/><ref name=memoriam/>

Van Dijk was married and had three children.

* {{cite book|title=Spherical functions on the þ-adic group PGL|publisher=North-Holland Publishing Company (N.V. Noord-Hollandsche Uitgevers Maatschappij)|location=Amsterdam|year=1969|lccn=70458330}} (doctoral disseration; summary in Dutch)
* with Mannes Poel: {{cite book|title=The GL(2n-1,R)-spherical representations of SL(2n,R)|publisher=University of Groningen|location=Groningen|year=1988}}
* as editor with Lambertus A. Pelletier: {{cite book|title=Thomas Joannes Stieltjes jr., 1856-1894: eredoctor van de Leidse Universiteit|publisher=Universiteit Leiden|year=1989}}
**''Oeuvres complètes = Collected papers / [par] Thomas Jan Stieltjes'' (reissue of the ''Oeuvres completes'' by Stieltjes (with a concise biography and commentaries by Gerrit van Dijk) published by Springer. Berlin/New York. 1993 {{LCCN|93009944}}
* {{cite book|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/28641665|title=Dat was afgesproken (That was agreed)|publisher=Universiteit Leiden|year=2004}} (emeritus farewell speech in Dutch) 
* {{cite book|title=Geloof in de wiskunde: over de getallen van Fibonacci in kunst en literatuur, hun goddelijke status en een discussie over religie en wiskunde (Faith in mathematics: on the Fibonacci numbers in art and literature, their divine status, and a discussion on religion and mathematics)|publisher=Koninklijke Hollandsche Maatschappij der Wetenschappen (Royal Dutch Society of Mathematics)|location=Haarlem|year=2006}}
* {{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IexDjWQz7oQC|title=Introduction to harmonic analysis and generalized Gelfand pairs|publisher=Walter de Gruyter|location=Berlin|year=2009|isbn=978-3-11-022019-3 }}<ref>{{cite web|author=Zaldivar, Felipe|date=June 5, 2010|url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/introduction-to-harmonic-analysis-and-generalized-gelfand-pairs |title=Review of ''Introduction to Harmonic Analysis and Generalized Gelfand Pairs'' by Gerrit van Dijk|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America }}</ref>
* as editor with Masato Wakayama: {{cite book|title=Casimir force, Casimir operators, and the Riemann hypothesis : mathematics for innovation in industry and science|location=Berlin; New York|publisher=De Gruyter|year=2010|lccn=2010031030|isbn=978-3110226126}}

* {{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JzFoHvXH_04C|title=Distribution theory: convolution, Fourier transform, and Laplace transform|location=Berlin|publisher=De Gruyter|year=2013|lccn=2012554713|isbn=978-3110295917}}<ref>{{cite web|author=Das, Tushar|date=February 22, 2014|title=Review of ''Distribution theory: convolution, Fourier transform, and Laplace transform'' by Gerrit van Dijk|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/distribution-theory-convolution-fourier-transform-and-laplace-transform}}</ref>
